samples.summary: New `cell()` nested-value serialization is only used/tested on the record path; the array path still uses `String()` and no test covers nested values in array rows
samples.evidence: `cell()` (table.ts:7-10) is documented as "Mirrors what `formatCsv` already does", but `formatTable`'s array branch (lines 46 and 53) still does `String(row[k] ?? '')`, so an array row containing an object still renders `[object Object]`. The only nested-value table test is `schema ctx.list --format table` (test/status.test.ts:236-241), which goes through `formatRecord`. output.test.ts's array-table tests use scalar-only rows (`{ a: 1 }`, etc.). Nothing would fail if the array path kept mis-rendering nested payloads.

samples.summary: `expect(table).not.toContain('[object Object]')` in the status table test is trivially true and does not exercise the nested-value handling it appears to guard
samples.evidence: `buildStatus(makeSession())` returns an entirely flat payload (status.ts buildStatus: only strings/booleans), so `format(..., 'table')` can never emit `[object Object]` regardless of whether `cell()`/`formatRecord` JSON-serialize nested values. The assertion passes even if the new nested-serialization logic were deleted. The real coverage for that behavior is the separate `schema ctx.list --format table` test; this one reads as coverage but is vacuous.

samples.summary: No test covers `formatRecord`/`cell` rendering of a null field — precisely the `workspaceName: null` case this diff introduces
samples.evidence: `buildStatus` can return `workspaceName: null` (status.ts) and the registry now advertises `'string | null'`. `cell(null)` returns `''` via `String(value ?? '')`. The only table assertion for status (test/status.test.ts:81-87) uses a session whose active workspace resolves, so workspaceName is a string; `buildStatus(makeSession({activeWorkspace:'missing-id'}))` is only asserted as JSON (lines 68-72). output.test.ts's new record tests use `{loggedIn:true,user:'hackerwins'}` and `{}` only. A regression printing `null` or `undefined` in the table would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: The `schema <unknown-command>` NOT_FOUND branch, relocated inside the new try/catch by this diff, has no test
samples.evidence: schema.ts still emits `{error:{code:'NOT_FOUND'...}}` and sets exitCode 1, and its position relative to `parseOutputFormat` is now behaviorally significant (format is validated first). test/schema.test.ts only exercises the registry functions (getCommandSchema/getAllCommandSchemas) and never drives the command; test/status.test.ts drives `schema --format bogus` and `schema ctx.list --format table` but never an unknown command name. Nothing asserts the NOT_FOUND body or exit code survived the refactor.

samples.summary: The new throwing `default:` branch in `format()` now fires for ~20 unmigrated `output(data, opts.format, ...)` call sites, none of which have a test for `--format bogus`
samples.evidence: `opts.format` is still passed unvalidated in cells.ts (4 sites), docs.ts (5), notes.ts (5), slides.ts (5), tabs.ts, api-keys.ts (3), sheets-import.ts. With the new `default: throw`, each of those now takes a completely new failure path (e.g. api-keys.ts:20 throws only after the one-time key has been created). The wiring suite only covers status, ctx list and schema, and its comment at test/status.test.ts:227-229 asserts "schema is the one other output() caller" — the behavior change is far broader than the tests.

samples.summary: No test asserts the registry's advertised `status` / `ctx.list` response shape matches what `buildStatus` / `buildWorkspaceList` actually emit
samples.evidence: The diff rewrites the `status` response schema (registry.ts:63-73) to mirror `StatusPayload`, and `ctx.list` advertises `{id,name,active}`. Nothing ties the two: test/schema.test.ts asserts only names/safety/parameters, and test/status.test.ts asserts payload keys without consulting the registry. A future field added to `buildStatus` (or renamed) leaves the advertised schema silently wrong — the exact drift this diff was fixing.

samples.summary: `honors status --format csv` asserts only the CSV header, not the data row
samples.evidence: The test checks `lastStdout().split('\n')[0] === 'loggedIn,message'`; the value row is never asserted, so a csv formatter that emitted a correct header with wrong/empty values would still pass. output.test.ts covers formatCsv separately, so this is only a breadth nit on the wiring test.

samples.summary: The `parseOutputFormat` rejection test's try/catch assertions are silently skipped if no throw occurs
samples.evidence: Lines 60-66: after `expect(() => ...).toThrow(InvalidFormatError)`, a second bare `try { parseOutputFormat('bogus') } catch (e) { ... }` holds the code/message assertions. If the function stopped throwing, the catch body never runs and those assertions vanish (no `expect.assertions(...)`). Harmless here because the preceding `toThrow` fails first, but the pattern is fragile.
